children: South Korea's bourse operator triggered a sell-side "sidecar" trading halt early Thursday as the benchmark KOSPI index plunged more than 5%, tracking a tech-led selloff on Wall Street, where sticky US inflation data fuelled more rate-hike bets.
The automatic five-minute suspension on program sell orders was activated after heavy losses in index futures, an abrupt cooling mechanism, as the KOSPI
was set for its seventh straight session of losses, its longest losing streak since September 2024.
The benchmark KOSPI was down 300.31 points, or 5.00%, at 5,708.50 as of 00:11 GMT. Chipmaker Samsung Electronics
fell 6.03%, while peer SK Hynix
lost 7.47%.
Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution
slid 3.44%, while Hyundai Motor
and sister automaker Kia Corp
were down 3.99% and down 2.03%, respectively.
Of the 889 issues traded, 90 shares advanced while 768 declined.
Foreigners were net sellers of shares worth 355.6 billion won.
The won was quoted at 1,339.5 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform
, up 0.21% from its previous close at 1,342.3.
In money and debt markets, December futures on three-year treasury bonds (KTBc1) gained 0.10 point to 102.98.
The most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond yield (KR3YT=RR) was flat at 3.885%, while the benchmark 10-year yield
was flat at 4.245%.
